findings.criterion: All — an unreadable plan cannot certify any criterion
findings.section: entire artifact (structure)
findings.message: This is the register item, STILL UNRESOLVED — and worse, the draft now asserts it is fixed while the artifact refutes the assertion on its face. The "Round-3 re-emission, deduplicated" contains: (a) raw search/replace conflict markers (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) in the body; (b) THREE copies of the North Star; (c) a full second copy of the master plan embedded mid-sentence inside launch-surface item 2 — the exact defect the changelog claims was "excised"; (d) the double phase numbering ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 —", "Phase 4 — Phase 3 —") the changelog claims was collapsed, including TWO distinct sections titled "Phase 4"; (e) a third full copy embedded inside changelog item 1, which recursively contains the corrupted round-2 artifact again. Consequence: Phases 4 (pricing), 5 (surfaces), and 6–7 exist ONLY inside embedded corrupted copies — the outer "clean" document terminates mid-Phase-3, so the canonical text serving criteria 2, 5, and 6 is not recoverable from a single authoritative sequence. Separately from readability, a changelog that reports "Corruption — FIXED" over an artifact that still contains it is itself an honesty defect in a plan whose entire theme is honest provenance. Not lockable in this state.

findings.criterion: 1 (swarm spend visible going forward) and 4 (history recovered)
findings.section: Phase 3 single-owner matrix + Phase 6 deferrals
findings.message: The single-owner matrix is presented as closed but has an unowned class: sessions that go TERMINAL between the Phase-0 snapshot and the Phase-3 deploy. Walk it: (a) they are not in the snapshot, so the Phase-6 backfill — which "reads the frozen snapshot exclusively" — reports them no-sidecar; (b) they HAVE registry rows, so the orphan-sidecar sweep ("no registry row") skips them; (c) they never had a finalize attempt under the new substrate, so there is no `finalize-deferred` record for the sweep to retry; (d) they are already terminal at deploy, so no reconcile-dead TRANSITION ever fires for them. Phase 6's deferral explicitly refuses a second backfill mode against the live root, claiming the orphan sweep covers post-snapshot dirs — false for registered sessions. The bitter irony a competitor would seize on: this population is guaranteed to be LARGE, because it is this effort's own multi-week Crucible/Foreman build, which spawns exactly the swarm sessions criterion 1 exists to measure. The plan's flagship population re-enacts the intake failure (registered, terminal, forever unmeasured) during its own construction. Fix direction: the sweep must also own "terminal registry session with NO usage record," reading the live sidecar root, not only `finalize-deferred` retries.

findings.criterion: 3 (a later live finalize can still measure) and 4
findings.section: Phase 1 repair path · Phase 3 terminality rule · Phase 0 exclusivity claim
findings.message: Three internal inconsistencies interlock around the deferred→archive path. First, the terminality rule has the sweep check whether a sidecar exists "in the live root and the Phase-0 archive" — so the sweep READS the archive, directly contradicting Phase 0's "the Phase 6 backfill tool points at this snapshot exclusively." Second, for a deferred record whose sidecar exists only in the archive, the sweep can see it but (per archive exclusivity) may not measure from it, and exhaustion never fires (sidecar not absent) — producing a by-design infinite retry loop every ~30 minutes for weeks until Phase 6, with two owners (sweep per the matrix, backfill per Phase 1's repair text) both claiming the same records. Third, Phase 1 promises "the Phase 6 backfill measures them [the 3 repaired sessions] through the normal claim path" without establishing that those sessions' sidecars exist in the archive at all — they were stamped `sidecar-root-unavailable`, i.e., the one population for which sidecar presence is precisely NOT evidenced. If absent from both roots, the terminality rule exhausts them to terminal `unmeasured` within ~10h of the Phase-3 deploy — weeks before Phase 6 — and the repair script's single-run latch forbids the only sanctioned resurrection path from running again. The plan must state which owner measures archive-only deferrals, and must condition the Phase-1 promise on verified archive presence.

findings.criterion: 1, 4, and Stage-0 decision 2 (measured-backfill "auditable forever")
findings.section: Phase 3 orphan-sidecar sweep + unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through · Phase 2 closed vocabulary
findings.message: `measured-backfill` was locked (decision 2) as the provenance of the ONE-SHOT historical recovery — that is what makes it "auditable forever." The plan then reuses the identical label for two permanently-ongoing forward mechanisms: orphan-sidecar sweep captures and unwrapped shared-cwd child records. After Phase 6, an auditor can no longer answer "was this record recovered by the audited historical backfill run, or minted last Tuesday by the sweep?" — the audit distinction decision 2 exists to preserve is destroyed by construction, and the CLOSED usage_state vocabulary (frozen in Phase 2) contains no `measured-swept`/`measured-late` value to fix it without a plan amendment. A competitor's telemetry product keeps ingestion-path provenance distinct as table stakes. Compounding this: since eager in-process finalize for agy-dispatch is explicitly deferred, the 106-of-111 swarm population — the stated reason criterion 1 exists — will land predominantly under this conflated label, meaning the headline deliverable ships with its provenance story blurred. Add a distinct forward-sweep provenance value to the closed vocabulary now, while it is still amendable at plan time.

findings.criterion: 2 (interactive spend renders on the dashboard and project window)
findings.section: Phase 5 surfaces (dashboard + project window rollup lines)
findings.message: The plan adds per-session spend aggregation (`measured_sessions`, general lines, usage_state distribution, "N measured of M") to the dashboard and project-window renders, backed by per-session cost files under `.anchor/run-costs/` — but says nothing about render-path cost. This codebase has a documented, dated incident of exactly this failure: the 2026-06-16 perf fix exists because a per-render full scan of a growing record directory pushed `GET /` past the health check's 5s timeout once the population hit ~1k, and the fix mandated targeted per-id lookups, never `list_records()`. The run-cost population starts at 111+ and grows monotonically with every swarm launch (plus synthetic `sidecar:<uuid>` child rows). A competitor plan — or this repo's own prior art — would specify the aggregation as cached/incremental (e.g., computed at finalize time and folded into the existing cached rollup) rather than scan-at-render. Absent that specification, Phase 5 is on rails to reintroduce the red-banner regression the CLAUDE.md perf note memorializes.

findings.criterion: 1 (measured records for new runs)
findings.section: Phase 2 evidence layer · Phase 3 launch-surface table
findings.message: Competitor press: the engine already emits authoritative usage at the source — the stream-json result envelope carries usage/cost (the plan's own `job_runner` row keeps envelope measurement for exactly this reason), and Claude Code supports telemetry export. Yet for the other WIRED non-interactive spawners (Gandalf shard jobs, summarizer runner calls — all stream-json paths through `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD`), the plan routes measurement through the sidecar-scraping stack: mtime-quiesce heuristics, a parser version fence, and a race against engine retention pruning. A competitor meters push-at-source where the source offers it and reserves file scraping for the paths that truly need it (interactive PTY sessions, unwrapped orphans, backfill). The plan never evaluates this split; adopting envelope-first for envelope-capable spawners would shrink the fragile surface the parser fence exists to defend. Refinement, not relitigation — the sidecar substrate remains necessary for the interactive and historical paths the North Star names.

findings.criterion: 6 (counting is honest)
findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through · Phase 5 honest counting / coverage report
findings.message: The unwrapped-sub-agent mechanism mints records whose `session_id` (`sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) corresponds to no registry session, while every counting surface is defined over registry sessions: honest counting renders "N measured of M total" with M = registry population, and the coverage report reports "the fraction of registry sessions measured." Child records therefore contribute tokens to effort/fleet sums but exist outside both the numerator-denominator contract and the coverage ratio — a reader can observe rollup token totals that exceed what the "N measured of M" sessions could account for, with no surface explaining the residue. Specify whether child rows count as sessions (and in which denominator) or are rendered as an explicit separate line (e.g., "+K unattributed sub-agent records"), so the honest-counting invariant stays literally checkable.

findings.criterion: 1 (finalize fires from both the owning orchestrator and reconcile-dead)
findings.section: Phase 1 beacon consume-time rule × Phase 3 eager owner finalize
findings.message: The strengthened beacon rule defeats Stage-0 decision 4. To consume the CAS a finalizer must "(a) BE the beacon-minting process this boot (PID + boot-token match against its own in-memory token) and (b) still HOLD the live exclusive bind." An owning orchestrator is a child `claude` process — it is never the process holding the 8777 bind, so under this rule EVERY eager owner finalize is structurally forced to `finalize-deferred`, collapsing the locked BOTH-paths design to sweep-only capture with up-to-30-minute latency, and making decision 4's eager path dead code. The plan never says how an orchestrator's finalize is proxied into the beaconed process (an HTTP call to the service? an in-process hook on session-end?). Either specify the proxy mechanism explicitly, or admit the eager path is really "the beaconed service finalizing on the session-end event" and rewrite the writer table row 1 to say so. As written, the two strongest sections of the plan contradict each other.

findings.criterion: 3 (a later live finalize can still measure)
findings.section: Phase 3 single-owner matrix + terminality
findings.message: The deferred→`unmeasured` terminality rule says "only the audited repair path may ever revisit it" — but the only repair path defined anywhere in the plan is hardcoded to an allowlist of exactly the 3 intake session ids and refuses a second run. The cited escape hatch is structurally unavailable for any record terminated by `DEFER_RETRY_MAX`. Concrete failure: a munging-function bug for one dirname class makes those sidecars look "absent" for 20 sweeps → records terminate at `unmeasured`; the bug is later fixed, the sidecars exist in the archive, and nothing can ever measure them — a software bug converted into permanent, unrepairable data loss, exactly the "burned latch" class criterion 3 exists to kill, just relocated from hermetic contexts to the sweep itself. Either define a general (still audited, still gated) re-open tool, or make exhaustion re-checkable when the correlation function version changes.

findings.criterion: 2 (interactive spend surfaces)
findings.section: Phase ordering / Phase 5
findings.message: Bored-investor core complaint: the one measured record (2.76M tok / 445s in `general`) exists TODAY, and rendering it as a separate rollup line is a surfaces-only change with zero dependency on the CAS, beacon, parser fence, or choke-point launcher — yet the plan gates it behind Phases 1–4. The stated justification ("surfaces render real substrate output, not placeholders") is vacuous for data that is already real substrate output. Criterion 2 could produce a visible dashboard receipt in the FIRST wave, de-risking the entire surfaces/consumer-enumeration work early and giving John a number on screen weeks sooner. The wave-ordering foresight optimizes soak time for the riskiest primitive but never weighs time-to-first-visible-value; a plan this long with the first dashboard pixel at Phase 5 is a sequencing choice that should be defended or changed, not defaulted.

findings.criterion: 6 (counting is honest)
findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped shared-cwd walk-through × Phase 5 honest counting
findings.message: Phase 3 mints synthetic child rows (`session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`, `parent_session_id: S`) for unwrapped sub-agents, and Phase 5 defines "N measured of M total" over registry sessions — but nothing specifies whether a child row is a "session" in either N or M. Both answers are wrong without a rule: counting them inflates M with entities that were never registry sessions (the exact inflation pathology criterion 6 targets, in a new costume); excluding them from N while summing their tokens makes token totals and session counts inconsistent on the same surface. The interaction is left for Stage 2 to improvise, in the one area the North Star explicitly says must be honest. Specify the counting rule for child records now.

findings.criterion: 4 (history recovered, honestly labeled)
findings.section: Phase 7 ship receipt / Phase 6 outcome expectations
findings.message: The final backfill receipt is "the coverage-report ratio moved" — an unfalsifiable gate. Moving from 0.9% to 1.8% "moved." The intake evidence gives the plan a quantified expectation it declines to use: ~55 sidecar dirs carry the deterministic marker against a 109-session target population, so the plan can and should state an expected-recovered band (e.g. "recovered ≈ the marker-bearing population; a shortfall >20% below the Phase-0 manifest count is an investigation trigger, not a shrug"). Without a numeric expectation, a backfill run that silently recovers 6 sessions because of a correlation bug still passes Phase 7. Honest labeling of outcomes is necessary but not sufficient — the ship gate must compare the outcome against what the intake evidence says should have been recoverable.

findings.criterion: 1 (swarm spend visible going forward)
findings.section: Phase 3 sweep cadence
findings.message: "After a long outage the first boot sweep catches up before engine pruning windows matter" is asserted with zero evidence about the engine's actual retention/pruning window — the very class of unverified assumption the plan forbids elsewhere. If the service is down (or the machine off) longer than the engine's pruning horizon, forward orphan sidecars are deleted before any sweep sees them, and those sessions become permanently invisible with no honest record (they never got a deferred stamp because they were never registered). Either cite the observed pruning behavior, or have the boot sweep mint honest `unmeasured` markers for registry sessions whose sidecars are gone, so the loss is visible rather than silent.

findings.criterion: 1, plus the safety-adjacency risk row
findings.section: Phase 3
findings.message: Phase 3 bundles the choke-point helper, five spawner-family wirings (including modifying the agy-dispatch skill outside this repo), observed-id readback, the zombie-hunter decouple (the plan's own named safety-critical adjacency), the widened sweep with terminality, the per-file orphan correlator, AND an interim production deploy — easily three waves of work under one header, with the safety-critical change buried mid-list. Every other phase is single-purpose. Concentrating the highest safety-adjacency risk and a live deploy in the same over-stuffed wave maximizes the chance the zombie-coverage gate gets run against a moving target. Split the zombie-decouple + its required gate into its own wave boundary.

findings.criterion: 3 — "a later live finalize can still measure"
findings.section: Phase 3 — Single-owner matrix + terminality; Phase 1 — repair script
findings.message: The terminality rule recreates the exact poison class this effort exists to kill, under a new name. Intake evidence proves sidecar-root unavailability is a real, transient condition (3 sessions stamped `sidecar-root-unavailable`). Under the new design that condition produces `finalize-deferred` (good), but the sweep then retries every ~30 min plus every boot; if the root stays unavailable across `DEFER_RETRY_MAX` = 20 sweeps (~10h of uptime — easily consumed in one day of dev-restart churn, since each deploy's boot sweep counts), the record transitions to terminal `unmeasured` and "a later sidecar appearance does not silently resurrect it; only the audited repair path may ever revisit it." But the only audited repair path in this plan is hardcoded to the 3 intake session ids AND single-run-latched — it refuses any other id and refuses a second run by construction. Net: root comes back, the data sits on disk, the record is permanently unmeasurable, and the future maintainer has zero sanctioned tool. The CAS file is technically unburned, but policy burns the latch anyway — criterion 3 violated in substance. The plan needs either evidence-based resurrection (sidecar appears → one audited un-terminal transition, logged) or a generalized repair CLI with the same admission discipline; the 3-id one-shot cannot be the only revisit mechanism.

findings.criterion: 1 and 4 — measured records must actually materialize; also the concurrency risk taxonomy
findings.section: Phase 2 closed vocabulary; Phase 3 single-owner matrix / sweep scope
findings.message: The vocabulary is closed but the state MACHINE is not. The sweep's scope is enumerated as exactly (a) reconcile-dead, (b) `finalize-deferred` retries, (c) orphan-sidecar scan. That leaves three states with no named owner, no retry rule, and no terminality: (i) `sidecar-format-unrecognized` is called "loud, retryable" — retryable by WHOM? It is not in (a)–(c), so when a future maintainer ships the parser fix after a CLI format change, no mechanism ever re-measures the accumulated unrecognized records; (ii) `id-unverified` appears in the vocabulary and nowhere else — is it terminal? displayed with tokens or without? swept? The matrix is silent; (iii) `measured-partial` consumes the exclusive-create claim, so an engine that stalls past the quiesce window and then finishes writing leaves a permanently undercounted record that append-only forbids ever completing — acceptable only if stated as a decision, which it isn't. Separately, the matrix's "exactly ONE owner" claim is already false for the 3 repaired records: they are pre-snapshot terminal sessions (owner: backfill CLI) that are simultaneously `finalize-deferred` (owner: the sweep, "the single named owner of deferred retries"), and whether the sweep can measure from the Phase-0 archive — or must sit in limbo until Phase 6 — is unspecified. The plan needs a complete transition table: every state × {owner, retry trigger, terminal?, display rule}.

findings.criterion: 3 (concurrency risk taxonomy: "double-write") and 2/6 (surfaces show honest numbers)
findings.section: Phase 1 CAS trust model rows 3–5 / closure invariant; Phase 3 decoupled finalize
findings.message: The plan hardens the claim FILE and then quietly designates the registry `usage_state` field as a second, unarbitrated write surface — "off-beacon contexts write only the registry's finalize-deferred field, which is not a claim file." That is the hole: an off-beacon writer (manual debug off-port, row 4) and the beaconed sweep race on the SAME registry record with no CAS. Sequence: sweep wins the claim, stamps `measured` on the registry; a lagging off-beacon finalize then stamps `finalize-deferred` over it — last-writer-wins regresses a measured record's visible state, the healthcheck deferral WARN flaps, and the sweep's retry hits an existing claim file with no defined reconciliation path back to `measured` (idempotent-content covers the cost file, not the registry field). This repo's history makes it concrete: non-atomic registry writes are a documented prior bug (rnd_registry corruption finding, 2026-07-08 review). The fix is cheap and must be stated: the claim/cost file is the single authoritative source of usage_state; the registry field is a derived cache the sweep reconciles, and no off-beacon writer may ever move a registry field FROM a measured state. Without that sentence, the top-listed risk (double-write) survives the mitigation built for it.

findings.criterion: 4 and Stage-0 decision 2 — "distinct provenance measured-backfill … auditable forever"
findings.section: Phase 3 orphan-sidecar sweep + unwrapped walk-through; Phase 2 closed vocabulary
findings.message: Decision 2 locked `measured-backfill` as the audit label for the ONE-SHOT historical recovery. Phase 3 then reuses the identical value for two permanent forward mechanisms: the ongoing orphan-sidecar sweep and every unwrapped shared-cwd child record. A future auditor asking "which numbers came from the July-2026 historical backfill?" — the exact auditability decision 2 promises "forever" — gets an unanswerable query: the label now means three different things (historical recovery, forward late-capture, synthetic child attribution) minted by two different owners across all future time. And the CLOSED vocabulary makes the obvious fix (a distinct `measured-sweep` / `measured-child` value) a plan-amendment event, so Stage 2 cannot quietly correct it. Either split the provenance values now, while the vocabulary is being frozen in the same document, or amend decision 2's "auditable forever" claim to match what the design actually preserves.

findings.criterion: 3 (hermetic predicate correctness) and 1 (measurement on legitimate hosts)
findings.section: Phase 1 redirect-seam list (CLOSED)
findings.message: The closed seam list includes "`ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` (stub runner)" with "ANY active seam forces the deferred path." The parenthetical hides an undefined discriminator. `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` is not hermetic-only: `lanes.detect_host_profile` treats a wired `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` as positive evidence of Claude availability, i.e. a legitimate production deployment (or the shareable distro this plan explicitly inherits seams to) may set it to a real wrapper. Two readings, both broken: (a) any-set forces deferral → a legit wrapper host defers EVERY finalize forever (sidecars present, so exhaustion never fires — permanent limbo, criterion 1 dead on that host class); (b) the code inspects the value to decide "stub" → that is name-sniffing, the exact anti-pattern this same plan bans for the synthetic-session predicate ("marker convention, never name-sniffing"). The seam entry needs a defined, testable predicate — e.g. an explicit `ANCHOR_HERMETIC=1` marker that fake_claude/test harnesses set, with `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` itself removed from the list — before `test_redirect_seam_forces_deferred` can even be written coherently.

findings.criterion: 1 — swarm spend visible; the 106-of-111 population
findings.section: Phase 3 launch-surface table item 5 / deferred
findings.message: The single most important launch surface (item 5, the agy-dispatch swarm — the population criterion 1 exists for) is the only one whose wiring lives OUTSIDE this repo: the wrapper adoption is a change to a Skill Foundry skill, unreachable by Anchor's raw-spawn conformance grep, Anchor's test suite, and Anchor's STUB-GATEs. The plan names the adoption as "a NAMED concrete task of this wave" but names no gate that proves it happened and no mechanism that catches its regression — a later skill edit that drops the env-pin consumption silently demotes the entire swarm population from eager `measured` to sweep-latency capture with (per Finding 5) backfill provenance forever, and the only signal is a slow drift in the coverage-report ratio that nothing alarms on. Minimum fix: a Phase-7 receipt item asserting the fleet run's sub-agent records carry `measured` (eager) provenance, not `measured-backfill` — making wrapper regression a visible receipt failure rather than a ratio whisper — plus a named healthcheck WARN threshold on the backfill-provenance fraction of new swarm records.

findings.criterion: 3 and the suite-contamination risk row
findings.section: Phase 1 closure invariant; Phase 3 conformance greps
findings.message: "The invariant is literally true OF the table because the test forces the table and the code to coincide" overstates what a grep can do. A grep conformance test detects textual patterns; a refactor that renames the helper, wraps `os.open` behind an alias, or moves the claim-dir constant defeats it silently and returns GREEN — the vacuous-GREEN failure mode this project has already logged twice (Doctor V3 wave-4; telemetry-resume). The greps are fine as tripwires, but the plan should stop calling them enforcement and add one structural backstop: a runtime assert in the claim-write helper that its caller module is on the writer allowlist (cheap, stdlib, survives renames), demoting the greps to what they are.

findings.criterion: 6 — honest counting
findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped walk-through vs Phase 5 honest counting
findings.message: Child records (`session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) are run-cost rows with no registry session. Phase 5's rule — "a session counts iff it contributed a measured record" and "'N measured of M total'" — is defined over registry sessions, so it is undefined whether child rows increment N, M, both, or neither. Sum-into-effort-totals (tokens) is specified; the SESSION-count denominator is not, and a maintainer wiring the rollup will guess. One sentence fixes it (e.g. children contribute tokens only, never counted as sessions, enumerated separately).

findings.section: Phase 1 beacon consume-time re-verification
findings.message: Condition (b) — "still HOLD the live exclusive bind at the moment of claim (re-probed on the listener handle)" — tests a state that cannot occur while the process holds an open `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` listener: possession of the open handle IS the bind; there is no "lost the port between mint and consume" transition short of the process closing the socket itself. `test_beacon_consume_reverify` therefore pins an unreachable path, and a future maintainer will burn time trying to construct it or, worse, add socket-closing shutdown logic to make the test honest. Either specify the real scenario intended (e.g. finalize running during shutdown after listener close — then say that) or drop condition (b) and keep the in-memory boot-token match, which alone makes an orphaned beacon file inert.

The plan then reuses the identical label for two permanently-ongoing forward mechanisms: orphan-sidecar sweep captures and unwrapped shared-cwd child records. After Phase 6, an auditor can no longer answer "was this record recovered by the audited historical backfill run, or minted last Tuesday by the sweep?" — the audit distinction decision 2 exists to preserve is destroyed by construction, and the CLOSED usage_state vocabulary (frozen in Phase 2) contains no `measured-swept`/`measured-late` value to fix it without a plan amendment. A competitor's telemetry product keeps ingestion-path provenance distinct as table stakes. Compounding this: since eager in-process finalize for agy-dispatch is explicitly deferred, the 106-of-111 swarm population — the stated reason criterion 1 exists — will land predominantly under this conflated label, meaning the headline deliverable ships with its provenance story blurred. Add a distinct forward-sweep provenance value to the closed vocabulary now, while it is still amendable at plan time.

findings.section: Phase 5 surfaces (dashboard + project window rollup lines)
findings.criterion: 2 (interactive spend renders on the dashboard and project window)
findings.message: The plan adds per-session spend aggregation (`measured_sessions`, general lines, usage_state distribution, "N measured of M") to the dashboard and project-window renders, backed by per-session cost files under `.anchor/run-costs/` — but says nothing about render-path cost. This codebase has a documented, dated incident of exactly this failure: the 2026-06-16 perf fix exists because a per-render full scan of a growing record directory pushed `GET /` past the health check's 5s timeout once the population hit ~1k, and the fix mandated targeted per-id lookups, never `list_records()`. The run-cost population starts at 111+ and grows monotonically with every swarm launch (plus synthetic `sidecar:<uuid>` child rows). A competitor plan — or this repo's own prior art — would specify the aggregation as cached/incremental (e.g., computed at finalize time and folded into the existing cached rollup) rather than scan-at-render. Absent that specification, Phase 5 is on rails to reintroduce the red-banner regression the CLAUDE.md perf note memorializes.

findings.topic: native engine usage emission ignored for wired spawners
findings.section: Phase 2 evidence layer · Phase 3 launch-surface table
findings.criterion: 1 (measured records for new runs)
findings.message: Competitor press: the engine already emits authoritative usage at the source — the stream-json result envelope carries usage/cost (the plan's own `job_runner` row keeps envelope measurement for exactly this reason), and Claude Code supports telemetry export. Yet for the other WIRED non-interactive spawners (Gandalf shard jobs, summarizer runner calls — all stream-json paths through `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD`), the plan routes measurement through the sidecar-scraping stack: mtime-quiesce heuristics, a parser version fence, and a race against engine retention pruning. A competitor meters push-at-source where the source offers it and reserves file scraping for the paths that truly need it (interactive PTY sessions, unwrapped orphans, backfill). The plan never evaluates this split; adopting envelope-first for envelope-capable spawners would shrink the fragile surface the parser fence exists to defend. Refinement, not relitigation — the sidecar substrate remains necessary for the interactive and historical paths the North Star names.

findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through · Phase 5 honest counting / coverage report
findings.criterion: 6 (counting is honest)
findings.message: The unwrapped-sub-agent mechanism mints records whose `session_id` (`sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) corresponds to no registry session, while every counting surface is defined over registry sessions: honest counting renders "N measured of M total" with M = registry population, and the coverage report reports "the fraction of registry sessions measured." Child records therefore contribute tokens to effort/fleet sums but exist outside both the numerator-denominator contract and the coverage ratio — a reader can observe rollup token totals that exceed what the "N measured of M" sessions could account for, with no surface explaining the residue. Specify whether child rows count as sessions (and in which denominator) or are rendered as an explicit separate line (e.g., "+K unattributed sub-agent records"), so the honest-counting invariant stays literally checkable.

reviews.note: Pressed through the bored-investor lens: three rounds in, the document is still not a shippable artifact, and the plan's value latency and receipt falsifiability are weaker than its mechanism prose suggests.

findings.section: entire draft (launch-surface table item 2; phase overview; trailing changelog)
findings.criterion: all — an unparseable plan cannot serve any criterion
findings.message: This register item is STILL UNRESOLVED, and worse, the changelog now falsely claims it fixed. The "Round-3 re-emission, deduplicated" emission contains: (a) launch-surface item 2 still broken mid-sentence — "envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)" — with an ENTIRE second copy of the document (North Star included) embedded inside the backtick span, then a dangling ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3)" stitch fragment; (b) the old double-numbered phase headers ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 —", "Phase 2 — Phase 1 —", and TWO headers titled "Phase 4") alive inside that embedded copy, plus a THIRD partial copy after the changelog begins; (c) raw unapplied search/replace markers (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) sitting in the text, including an unmerged edit that leaves BOTH "Seven phases" and "Eight phases, numbered 0–7" as competing overview sentences. The changelog's claim "Exactly ONE North Star copy remains" is verifiably false of this very emission — there are at least three. A plan whose own changelog misreports its content fails the honesty standard the plan preaches on every page. As a bored investor: three rounds have been spent on re-emission mechanics and the deliverable is still not a document a Foreman wave can be cut from. Not lockable.

findings.section: Phase 1 beacon consume-time rule × Phase 3 eager owner finalize
findings.criterion: 1 (finalize fires from both the owning orchestrator and reconcile-dead)
findings.message: The strengthened beacon rule defeats Stage-0 decision 4. To consume the CAS a finalizer must "(a) BE the beacon-minting process this boot (PID + boot-token match against its own in-memory token) and (b) still HOLD the live exclusive bind." An owning orchestrator is a child `claude` process — it is never the process holding the 8777 bind, so under this rule EVERY eager owner finalize is structurally forced to `finalize-deferred`, collapsing the locked BOTH-paths design to sweep-only capture with up-to-30-minute latency, and making decision 4's eager path dead code. The plan never says how an orchestrator's finalize is proxied into the beaconed process (an HTTP call to the service? an in-process hook on session-end?). Either specify the proxy mechanism explicitly, or admit the eager path is really "the beaconed service finalizing on the session-end event" and rewrite the writer table row 1 to say so. As written, the two strongest sections of the plan contradict each other.

findings.section: Phase 3 single-owner matrix + terminality
findings.criterion: 3 (a later live finalize can still measure)
findings.message: The deferred→`unmeasured` terminality rule says "only the audited repair path may ever revisit it" — but the only repair path defined anywhere in the plan is hardcoded to an allowlist of exactly the 3 intake session ids and refuses a second run. The cited escape hatch is structurally unavailable for any record terminated by `DEFER_RETRY_MAX`. Concrete failure: a munging-function bug for one dirname class makes those sidecars look "absent" for 20 sweeps → records terminate at `unmeasured`; the bug is later fixed, the sidecars exist in the archive, and nothing can ever measure them — a software bug converted into permanent, unrepairable data loss, exactly the "burned latch" class criterion 3 exists to kill, just relocated from hermetic contexts to the sweep itself. Either define a general (still audited, still gated) re-open tool, or make exhaustion re-checkable when the correlation function version changes.

findings.section: Phase ordering / Phase 5
findings.criterion: 2 (interactive spend surfaces)
findings.message: Bored-investor core complaint: the one measured record (2.76M tok / 445s in `general`) exists TODAY, and rendering it as a separate rollup line is a surfaces-only change with zero dependency on the CAS, beacon, parser fence, or choke-point launcher — yet the plan gates it behind Phases 1–4. The stated justification ("surfaces render real substrate output, not placeholders") is vacuous for data that is already real substrate output. Criterion 2 could produce a visible dashboard receipt in the FIRST wave, de-risking the entire surfaces/consumer-enumeration work early and giving John a number on screen weeks sooner. The wave-ordering foresight optimizes soak time for the riskiest primitive but never weighs time-to-first-visible-value; a plan this long with the first dashboard pixel at Phase 5 is a sequencing choice that should be defended or changed, not defaulted.

findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped shared-cwd walk-through × Phase 5 honest counting
findings.criterion: 6 (counting is honest)
findings.message: Phase 3 mints synthetic child rows (`session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`, `parent_session_id: S`) for unwrapped sub-agents, and Phase 5 defines "N measured of M total" over registry sessions — but nothing specifies whether a child row is a "session" in either N or M. Both answers are wrong without a rule: counting them inflates M with entities that were never registry sessions (the exact inflation pathology criterion 6 targets, in a new costume); excluding them from N while summing their tokens makes token totals and session counts inconsistent on the same surface. The interaction is left for Stage 2 to improvise, in the one area the North Star explicitly says must be honest. Specify the counting rule for child records now.

findings.section: Phase 7 ship receipt / Phase 6 outcome expectations
findings.criterion: 4 (history recovered, honestly labeled)
findings.message: The final backfill receipt is "the coverage-report ratio moved" — an unfalsifiable gate. Moving from 0.9% to 1.8% "moved." The intake evidence gives the plan a quantified expectation it declines to use: ~55 sidecar dirs carry the deterministic marker against a 109-session target population, so the plan can and should state an expected-recovered band (e.g. "recovered ≈ the marker-bearing population; a shortfall >20% below the Phase-0 manifest count is an investigation trigger, not a shrug"). Without a numeric expectation, a backfill run that silently recovers 6 sessions because of a correlation bug still passes Phase 7. Honest labeling of outcomes is necessary but not sufficient — the ship gate must compare the outcome against what the intake evidence says should have been recoverable.

findings.section: Phase 3 sweep cadence
findings.criterion: 1 (swarm spend visible going forward)
findings.message: "After a long outage the first boot sweep catches up before engine pruning windows matter" is asserted with zero evidence about the engine's actual retention/pruning window — the very class of unverified assumption the plan forbids elsewhere. If the service is down (or the machine off) longer than the engine's pruning horizon, forward orphan sidecars are deleted before any sweep sees them, and those sessions become permanently invisible with no honest record (they never got a deferred stamp because they were never registered). Either cite the observed pruning behavior, or have the boot sweep mint honest `unmeasured` markers for registry sessions whose sidecars are gone, so the loss is visible rather than silent.

findings.section: Phase 3
findings.criterion: 1, plus the safety-adjacency risk row
findings.message: Phase 3 bundles the choke-point helper, five spawner-family wirings (including modifying the agy-dispatch skill outside this repo), observed-id readback, the zombie-hunter decouple (the plan's own named safety-critical adjacency), the widened sweep with terminality, the per-file orphan correlator, AND an interim production deploy — easily three waves of work under one header, with the safety-critical change buried mid-list. Every other phase is single-purpose. Concentrating the highest safety-adjacency risk and a live deploy in the same over-stuffed wave maximizes the chance the zombie-coverage gate gets run against a moving target. Split the zombie-decouple + its required gate into its own wave boundary.

reviews.note: Reviewed through the future-maintainer lens as directed. The register item (corruption) is re-checked first and is STILL unresolved despite the changelog claiming it fixed; remaining findings are new failure modes in the state machine, ownership matrix, and enforcement story that a maintainer inherits after this effort ships.

findings.section: whole document / Round-3 mechanical note / changelog item 1
findings.criterion: all — the plan is the Foreman handoff artifact; unresolvable Phase-N references and a false changelog break execution of every criterion
findings.message: KNOWN register item, explicitly STILL UNRESOLVED — and now compounded by a false fix claim. The mechanical note asserts "ONE North Star copy, ONE copy of each phase, single phase numbering 0–7, launch-surface item 2 restored intact." The artifact contradicts every clause: the North Star appears at least three times; literal merge/search-replace markers (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) survive in the body; a full second copy of the draft is still embedded mid-sentence inside launch-surface item 2 ("envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)…"), which is therefore NOT restored intact; the embedded copies carry the double numbering ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 —", "Phase 4 — Phase 3 —") alongside a competing "## Phase 4 — Pricing engine", so "Phase 4" resolves to two different phases depending on which copy a builder lands in. Worse than the corruption itself is the changelog stating "Corruption (the not-lockable cause) — FIXED" over a document that visibly refutes it: a future maintainer (or Foreman) who trusts the changelog will execute against whichever copy they hit first. This cannot lock until a genuinely clean emission exists and the changelog claims only what the bytes show.

findings.section: Phase 3 — Single-owner matrix + terminality; Phase 1 — repair script
findings.criterion: 3 — "a later live finalize can still measure"
findings.message: The terminality rule recreates the exact poison class this effort exists to kill, under a new name. Intake evidence proves sidecar-root unavailability is a real, transient condition (3 sessions stamped `sidecar-root-unavailable`). Under the new design that condition produces `finalize-deferred` (good), but the sweep then retries every ~30 min plus every boot; if the root stays unavailable across `DEFER_RETRY_MAX` = 20 sweeps (~10h of uptime — easily consumed in one day of dev-restart churn, since each deploy's boot sweep counts), the record transitions to terminal `unmeasured` and "a later sidecar appearance does not silently resurrect it; only the audited repair path may ever revisit it." But the only audited repair path in this plan is hardcoded to the 3 intake session ids AND single-run-latched — it refuses any other id and refuses a second run by construction. Net: root comes back, the data sits on disk, the record is permanently unmeasurable, and the future maintainer has zero sanctioned tool. The CAS file is technically unburned, but policy burns the latch anyway — criterion 3 violated in substance. The plan needs either evidence-based resurrection (sidecar appears → one audited un-terminal transition, logged) or a generalized repair CLI with the same admission discipline; the 3-id one-shot cannot be the only revisit mechanism.

findings.section: Phase 2 closed vocabulary; Phase 3 single-owner matrix / sweep scope
findings.criterion: 1 and 4 — measured records must actually materialize; also the concurrency risk taxonomy
findings.message: The vocabulary is closed but the state MACHINE is not. The sweep's scope is enumerated as exactly (a) reconcile-dead, (b) `finalize-deferred` retries, (c) orphan-sidecar scan. That leaves three states with no named owner, no retry rule, and no terminality: (i) `sidecar-format-unrecognized` is called "loud, retryable" — retryable by WHOM? It is not in (a)–(c), so when a future maintainer ships the parser fix after a CLI format change, no mechanism ever re-measures the accumulated unrecognized records; (ii) `id-unverified` appears in the vocabulary and nowhere else — is it terminal? displayed with tokens or without? swept? The matrix is silent; (iii) `measured-partial` consumes the exclusive-create claim, so an engine that stalls past the quiesce window and then finishes writing leaves a permanently undercounted record that append-only forbids ever completing — acceptable only if stated as a decision, which it isn't. Separately, the matrix's "exactly ONE owner" claim is already false for the 3 repaired records: they are pre-snapshot terminal sessions (owner: backfill CLI) that are simultaneously `finalize-deferred` (owner: the sweep, "the single named owner of deferred retries"), and whether the sweep can measure from the Phase-0 archive — or must sit in limbo until Phase 6 — is unspecified. The plan needs a complete transition table: every state × {owner, retry trigger, terminal?, display rule}.

findings.section: Phase 1 CAS trust model rows 3–5 / closure invariant; Phase 3 decoupled finalize
findings.criterion: 3 (concurrency risk taxonomy: "double-write") and 2/6 (surfaces show honest numbers)
findings.message: The plan hardens the claim FILE and then quietly designates the registry `usage_state` field as a second, unarbitrated write surface — "off-beacon contexts write only the registry's finalize-deferred field, which is not a claim file." That is the hole: an off-beacon writer (manual debug off-port, row 4) and the beaconed sweep race on the SAME registry record with no CAS. Sequence: sweep wins the claim, stamps `measured` on the registry; a lagging off-beacon finalize then stamps `finalize-deferred` over it — last-writer-wins regresses a measured record's visible state, the healthcheck deferral WARN flaps, and the sweep's retry hits an existing claim file with no defined reconciliation path back to `measured` (idempotent-content covers the cost file, not the registry field). This repo's history makes it concrete: non-atomic registry writes are a documented prior bug (rnd_registry corruption finding, 2026-07-08 review). The fix is cheap and must be stated: the claim/cost file is the single authoritative source of usage_state; the registry field is a derived cache the sweep reconciles, and no off-beacon writer may ever move a registry field FROM a measured state. Without that sentence, the top-listed risk (double-write) survives the mitigation built for it.

findings.section: Phase 3 orphan-sidecar sweep + unwrapped walk-through; Phase 2 closed vocabulary
findings.criterion: 4 and Stage-0 decision 2 — "distinct provenance measured-backfill … auditable forever"
findings.message: Decision 2 locked `measured-backfill` as the audit label for the ONE-SHOT historical recovery. Phase 3 then reuses the identical value for two permanent forward mechanisms: the ongoing orphan-sidecar sweep and every unwrapped shared-cwd child record. A future auditor asking "which numbers came from the July-2026 historical backfill?" — the exact auditability decision 2 promises "forever" — gets an unanswerable query: the label now means three different things (historical recovery, forward late-capture, synthetic child attribution) minted by two different owners across all future time. And the CLOSED vocabulary makes the obvious fix (a distinct `measured-sweep` / `measured-child` value) a plan-amendment event, so Stage 2 cannot quietly correct it. Either split the provenance values now, while the vocabulary is being frozen in the same document, or amend decision 2's "auditable forever" claim to match what the design actually preserves.

findings.section: Phase 1 redirect-seam list (CLOSED)
findings.criterion: 3 (hermetic predicate correctness) and 1 (measurement on legitimate hosts)
findings.message: The closed seam list includes "`ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` (stub runner)" with "ANY active seam forces the deferred path." The parenthetical hides an undefined discriminator. `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` is not hermetic-only: `lanes.detect_host_profile` treats a wired `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` as positive evidence of Claude availability, i.e. a legitimate production deployment (or the shareable distro this plan explicitly inherits seams to) may set it to a real wrapper. Two readings, both broken: (a) any-set forces deferral → a legit wrapper host defers EVERY finalize forever (sidecars present, so exhaustion never fires — permanent limbo, criterion 1 dead on that host class); (b) the code inspects the value to decide "stub" → that is name-sniffing, the exact anti-pattern this same plan bans for the synthetic-session predicate ("marker convention, never name-sniffing"). The seam entry needs a defined, testable predicate — e.g. an explicit `ANCHOR_HERMETIC=1` marker that fake_claude/test harnesses set, with `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` itself removed from the list — before `test_redirect_seam_forces_deferred` can even be written coherently.

findings.section: Phase 3 launch-surface table item 5 / deferred
findings.criterion: 1 — swarm spend visible; the 106-of-111 population
findings.message: The single most important launch surface (item 5, the agy-dispatch swarm — the population criterion 1 exists for) is the only one whose wiring lives OUTSIDE this repo: the wrapper adoption is a change to a Skill Foundry skill, unreachable by Anchor's raw-spawn conformance grep, Anchor's test suite, and Anchor's STUB-GATEs. The plan names the adoption as "a NAMED concrete task of this wave" but names no gate that proves it happened and no mechanism that catches its regression — a later skill edit that drops the env-pin consumption silently demotes the entire swarm population from eager `measured` to sweep-latency capture with (per Finding 5) backfill provenance forever, and the only signal is a slow drift in the coverage-report ratio that nothing alarms on. Minimum fix: a Phase-7 receipt item asserting the fleet run's sub-agent records carry `measured` (eager) provenance, not `measured-backfill` — making wrapper regression a visible receipt failure rather than a ratio whisper — plus a named healthcheck WARN threshold on the backfill-provenance fraction of new swarm records.

findings.section: Phase 1 closure invariant; Phase 3 conformance greps
findings.criterion: 3 and the suite-contamination risk row
findings.message: "The invariant is literally true OF the table because the test forces the table and the code to coincide" overstates what a grep can do. A grep conformance test detects textual patterns; a refactor that renames the helper, wraps `os.open` behind an alias, or moves the claim-dir constant defeats it silently and returns GREEN — the vacuous-GREEN failure mode this project has already logged twice (Doctor V3 wave-4; telemetry-resume). The greps are fine as tripwires, but the plan should stop calling them enforcement and add one structural backstop: a runtime assert in the claim-write helper that its caller module is on the writer allowlist (cheap, stdlib, survives renames), demoting the greps to what they are.

findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped walk-through vs Phase 5 honest counting
findings.criterion: 6 — honest counting
findings.message: Child records (`session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) are run-cost rows with no registry session. Phase 5's rule — "a session counts iff it contributed a measured record" and "'N measured of M total'" — is defined over registry sessions, so it is undefined whether child rows increment N, M, both, or neither. Sum-into-effort-totals (tokens) is specified; the SESSION-count denominator is not, and a maintainer wiring the rollup will guess. One sentence fixes it (e.g. children contribute tokens only, never counted as sessions, enumerated separately).

findings.section: Phase 1 beacon consume-time re-verification
findings.message: Condition (b) — "still HOLD the live exclusive bind at the moment of claim (re-probed on the listener handle)" — tests a state that cannot occur while the process holds an open `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` listener: possession of the open handle IS the bind; there is no "lost the port between mint and consume" transition short of the process closing the socket itself. `test_beacon_consume_reverify` therefore pins an unreachable path, and a future maintainer will burn time trying to construct it or, worse, add socket-closing shutdown logic to make the test honest. Either specify the real scenario intended (e.g. finalize running during shutdown after listener close — then say that) or drop condition (b) and keep the in-memory boot-token match, which alone makes an orphaned beacon file inert.
